items.evidence: The notes never mention the opening or the agenda; they start at 'Market Research Findings'.

'75% of 100 subjects found remotes ugly; 80% willing to pay more', 'Losing the remote (50%+ cited as biggest issue)', 'Too many buttons', 'Users only use 10% of available buttons; most common actions are channel and volume changes', 'Desire for voice recognition inversely related to age: 15-35 age group most interested'. Not attributed to the marketing expert, but every finding is there.

'Remote is a communication device: user input -> chip -> infrared signal -> TV receiver' covers how a remote works, but the user interface designer's method (design specifications, several prototypes, user feedback, conventional layout with room for novelty, technology and price constraints) is absent.
No mention of the two example remotes (fully featured engineering design vs basic design) or their advantages and disadvantages.

'Four core components: 1. Energy source 2. Chip 3. User interface 4. Infrared bulb', 'Infrared chosen over alternatives: no line-of-sight required', 'Chip quality critical for clean signal transmission'. Not attributed to the industrial designer by name.

'Scope confirmed: TV only...; no teletext', 'Corporate identity: yellow and black...', 'Target group: broad appeal, roughly under 65', 'Voice recognition ruled out', 'Find-it locator feature', 'Rechargeable cradle ... proposed'.
'Post-meeting: each team member to complete a questionnaire and summary'.
'then 30 minutes individual work'.

'Upload presentations to shared project folder' has no owner and does not mention the minutes; the transcript has the project manager saying 'I'll make sure to put up the minutes and the project documentation and including these PowerPoint slides'.
'Upload presentations to shared project folder' is stated without saying the team members are to do it ('If everyone could do that as well').
'Individual workstreams: components concept (ID)'.
'user interface concept' is listed but the owner (user interface designer) is not stated.
'market trend watching' is listed but the owner (marketing expert) is not stated.
'no teletext (superseded by internet)'.
'Scope confirmed: TV only, no video or other devices'.
'Corporate identity: yellow and black color scheme, emphasis on the Rs in branding, must be visible in final design'. The slogan is not mentioned, but the requirement is captured.
'Core emphasis: simplicity and fashion'.

'age segmentation less useful than lifestyle/attitude targeting' gets the direction but not the decision as stated: the project manager said it is more useful to define objectives like fashion and simplicity than a specific age group, and the alternative floated was income / TV ownership, not lifestyle or attitude.
'Find-it locator feature (button on TV to make remote beep)'.
'Large accessible buttons for core functions'.
'Hidden/less prominent secondary functions' under agreed functions.
'Secondary/advanced functions hidden or less prominent, possibly behind a sliding panel'.

'Rechargeable cradle (like a phone dock) proposed as alternative' and 'Rechargeable or long-life battery solution' hedge it; the transcript has the project manager say 'that's a good idea, we'll keep it'.

'Target group: broad appeal, roughly under 65; age segmentation less useful' reflects the outcome, but the notes do not convey that settling the target group was an open difficulty ('It's hard to narrow it down').
'Voice recognition ruled out: too expensive, not essential for a remote'.
'Chip quality critical for clean signal transmission' touches it, but the question of how to make infra-red more functional (battery plus chip and component quality) is not framed as an issue.
'Rechargeable cradle (like a phone dock) proposed as alternative to disposable batteries' and 'Battery?' discussion captured as 'Rechargeable or long-life battery solution'.

errors.claim: Working design presentation not yet on the server; save from email into shared folder.
errors.why_wrong: The transcript shows the industrial designer's working design presentation is already in the shared folder ('technical functions presentation, working design presentation and the functional requirements'); the file that is only in email is the project manager's own document.

errors.claim: age segmentation less useful than lifestyle/attitude targeting
errors.why_wrong: Nobody proposed lifestyle or attitude targeting; the marketing expert suggested defining the group by how much money they have to spend and how recently they bought a television, and the project manager concluded it is more useful to define objectives like fashion and simplicity.
